title: Stop Renting Your AI's Memory — Dylan Couzon, Qdrant
talk_summary: A Qdrant DevRel talk arguing that AI memory should be owned locally rather than rented from cloud providers, using an embedded vector store (write/retrieve/forget) to give agents persistent, portable, queryable memory. The demo shows a fully offline drone object-detection memory with sub-millisecond semantic search over ~300 vectors in 15MB.

takeaways.technique: Embedded local vector store for agent memory
takeaways.what_they_do: Embed memories with payloads into an in-process vector store, query offline in milliseconds, with filtering by topic and decay by recency/frequency instead of dumping everything into a prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: retrieving the right memory beats dumping everything and praying the model finds it
takeaways.numbers: 1M memories < 1GB with quantization; demo: 300 vectors, 15MB, <1ms query

takeaways.what_they_do: Treat memory as three verbs: write new facts, retrieve relevant ones, and forget/decay stale ones by recency and frequency, rather than accumulating an ever-growing prompt.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's a system with three verbs: write, retrieve, and forget.

takeaways.what_they_do: Keep memory in a folder keyed by embedding model so swapping the reasoning model or hardware preserves continuity.
takeaways.evidence_quote: Swap the reasoning model, change the hardware, none of it matters. It all comes with you.
